kanji_index.target_note: Approximately 100. JLPT publishes no official kanji list, so membership at the edges is a judgement call.
kanji_index.pacing_note: 3–5 new kanji per content lesson through Unit 7, tapering to 0–3 in Units 8–9, where the conjugation load is highest.

vocabulary_plan.note: The lesson format allows 8–14 new words per content lesson, so the course itself reaches roughly 480 actively taught words. The remaining distance to the approximate 800-word N5 range is covered by the level wrap-up deck (WRAP N5) as recognition vocabulary.

spiral_review_plan: Every content lesson recycles at least 20% of its examples and questions from earlier lessons, listed in recycled_from.
Each lesson's first practice question revisits the previous lesson; each challenge set includes one item from a previous unit.
Words first taught in kana are re-shown in kanji form in the lesson that introduces their kanji, then used in kanji from then on.
Location words, あります / います, and food vocabulary from Units 2–3 are deliberately reused in Units 6 and 7.
The て-form (Unit 8) is the base for the た-form (Unit 9), so Unit 9 opens each lesson with て-form retrieval.

checkpoint_plan.per_unit: One review lesson with no new vocabulary, grammar, or kanji, then a 15-question assessment (pass at 12/15).
checkpoint_plan.per_level: WRAP N5: cumulative vocabulary and kanji decks, a grammar summary sheet, and a full mock exam in the three exam sections (言語知識, 読解, 聴解 scripts) with score interpretation.
checkpoint_plan.reading: Optional in N5. Short readings are planned for the review lessons of Units 6–9 so learners meet the reading screen before N4.

deviations_and_assumptions: Unit 1 is treated as fixed with 6 content lessons and no review lesson; the 5 + 1 shape applies from Unit 4.

Units 1–3 follow a can-do order that already introduced たべます / のみます, frequency adverbs, どんな, あります / います, 〜つ counters and ordering phrases earlier than a grammar-first textbook would. Unit 4 onward does not re-teach them; it extends them to new verbs and contexts.
Verb conjugation is introduced as a system in Unit 4 (ます / ません), although two verbs were met in Unit 2.
Comparisons (より / ほうが / いちばん) are placed in Unit 7 with shopping, earlier than in a grammar-first order, because choosing between items is the natural context and adjectives are complete by Unit 6.
The て-form is held until Unit 8 so that polite present, past, adjectives and counters are stable first.

Plain forms are limited to Unit 9: dictionary, ない and た forms, each tied to one polite pattern, plus one lesson of casual speech. Plain-form subordinate clauses (〜と おもいます, noun-modifying clauses) are deferred to N4 Unit 1.
Weekday names are written 月よう日 etc., because 曜 is not taught at this level.
Kanji whose level placement varies between published lists are included here as N5 by judgement: 駅, 社, 花, 魚, 道, 空, 耳. Any of them can move to N4 Unit 1 without affecting grammar order.

The rule that every new kanji appears in at least two taught words is checked when each lesson is written and enforced by the import step. If a kanji cannot be given two natural words in its lesson (candidates at risk: 火, 土, 目, 耳, 道), it moves to a later lesson rather than being forced.
Kanji readings, meanings and stroke counts in lesson output are advisory; the import step takes them from the site's dictionary source.
Estimated hours assume about 6 hours of study per week and bring N5 to roughly 150 hours in total including Units 1–3 and kana.
required_xp_level is null for every unit, as instructed.
No learner-facing content names any textbook; the references fields are internal.
